target_customer: Construction contractors, subcontractors and developers in the US
problem: Buying and tracking building materials is manual and a leading cause of late and over-budget projects.
business_model: Software subscription plus a procurement fee (2 to 5 percent on its turnkey service per company site)
product_category: Construction procurement and material management software

founders.name: Robert Salvador
prior_employers: SLP commercial construction company (founder and president, per YC page)
previous_startups: PoliTech.AI (co-founder and CEO, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Refresh Miami says he comes from a family of contractors and worked as one

founders.name: April Moss
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Refresh Miami July 2022; not listed on YC page

founders.name: Ivan Franco
founders.background_notes: Refresh Miami describes him as a blockchain expert

competitors.name: Agora (later Kojo)
competitors.what: Materials procurement platform for commercial construction

competitors.name: StructShare
competitors.what: Cloud platform for specialty contractor supply chains
competitors.funding_then: $8M raised, date per ENR article not confirmed in snippet

technical_complexity.rationale: Procurement workflow software with supplier integrations; later LLM features are standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with Procore, Sage and QuickBooks create modest lock-in; better-funded rivals already existed in 2021.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows Procore or others copying the wedge; Agora/Kojo kept scaling with far more capital.

market_need_then: Company cites 70 to 80 percent of projects running late or over budget and materials prices up 20 percent since 2020; vendor claims, not independently verified.

branding.brand_signature: Made By Builders, For Builders tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Local Miami press and trade mentions only; name is generic and shared with unrelated DigiBuild entities in aggregator results.

outcome_analysis: DigiBuild pairs a contractor founder with a procurement product, raised 4 million dollars in July 2022 and a 1.3 million extension in 2023, and reports named contractor customers. It stayed small and seed-funded by 2025 coverage, with a Series A only hinted at, so it is a modest survivor rather than a breakout.
notes: The company site says YC S'22 while YC lists Summer 2021; unresolved. Extension date 2023-05 is from CB Insights only, so only the year is used. A profile calls Salvador 'Fmr Founder & CEO'; leadership change unconfirmed. Totals of $5M to $6.7M vary by aggregator. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Competitor rivals found via search; Agora is dated by its Aug 2021 release; StructShare date not confirmed.
